stem.text: The specific heat capacity of different substances is shown.

A.text: Air is a more stable environment than water because it is more resistant to changes in temperature.

B.text: It takes more energy to raise the temperature of hydrogen gas than it does to raise the temperature of water.

C.text: A specific heat capacity of $4.2\,\text{J g}^{-1}\,{}^{\circ}\text{C}$ means that it takes $4.2\,\text{J}$ of energy to vaporise $1.0\,\text{g}$ of liquid water.

D.text: There are more hydrogen bonds between water molecules in a gas than between water molecules in a liquid.
